_maintainer_note: How much scaffolding each brain needs. BuildBot has no native tool-calling, so tool routing is done with keyword rulepacks plus prompt-shaped structure, and how much of that a model needs depends on the model. Rules, so this stays honest as models rotate: (1) routing_tier is the amount of scaffolding, not a quality score - 'light' means the model can be trusted to pick its own way through a request, 'guided' means it needs one step at a time, 'rails' means only the set phrasings work. (2) budgets are CEILINGS. A caller may ask for less; it can never be handed more than the profile allows, so a small brain is never given a context it will quietly truncate. (3) basis is 'measured:<silicon_id>' ONLY for a model we have actually benched on that board (see config/model_catalog.json 'silicon'). Today that is exactly one pair: qwen3:30b-a3b on jetson_agx_orin_64gb. Everything else is 'conservative-default' and must say so. Never invent a measured number. (4) limits_note is one plain sentence the bot or the wizard can say out loud about what this tier cannot do. Write it for a person, not a spec sheet. (5) '_default' is what an unknown or user-supplied model gets: the safe middle, never the light tier. Add a profile when you add a model to the catalog; if you have not benched it, 'conservative-default' is the correct and honest answer.
